newsitem.title: JAPAN: KDD says cable to save 10 bln yen in NTT charges.
newsitem.headline: KDD says cable to save 10 bln yen in NTT charges.

text.p: Kokusai Denshin Denwa Co Ltd said on Thursday that its planned undersea fibre optic cable around Japan would save it 10 billion yen a year in charges it pays to Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp for using its local call network.
KDD president Tadashi Nishimoto told a news conference that KDD currently pays about 30 billion yen a year to NTT in access charges.
He said the fibre optic cable around three of Japan's main islands would cut the charges by about 10 billion yen a year.
KDD, Japan's largest international telecommunications carrier, said earlier that the cost of constructing the cable would be 130 billion yen.
It said construction would start in the middle of this year and the system would begin operating at the end of March 1999.
The 8,500 km cable will loop around the islands of Honshu, Shikoku and Kyushu.
KDD said in October that the cable would have a capacity of 100 gigabits, or 1.2 million phone lines, and help it lower its international call charges.
